metadata.title: PISA for Development Assessment and Analytical Framework: Reading, Mathematics and Science

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA-D framework document describes assessment design, instruments, and questionnaire content rather than reporting an empirical analysis with an analytic dataset. It specifies that PISA-D uses school-based and out-of-school components, with paper-based school tests and tablet-based out-of-school tests, and that students complete background questionnaires (and schools/teachers complete additional questionnaires). The document does not provide any sampling-weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so weighting cannot be confirmed from the text. For analysts using PISA/PISA-D microdata, complex survey design weights and plausible-value scaling are typically required to produce population-representative estimates and correct standard errors, but this framework publication itself does not specify the exact weight variables or replicate design implementation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a framework and assessment design publication, not an empirical study predicting or estimating student outcomes from microdata. As such, it does not report a dependent variable based on plausible values (PV-based achievement scores) nor any missing-data handling procedure for an analytic model. The absence of PV and missing-data methodology is therefore by design: the text focuses on what is assessed, how domains are defined, and how instruments and questionnaires are structured for future implementation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is not an empirical analysis paper; it provides planned/expected sample coverage for PISA-D implementation. It states that the school-based component targets about 37,100 students (representing about 1,200,000 15-year-olds in Grade 7 or above) across seven participating countries, and that the out-of-school component targets about 16,200 youth (representing about 1,700,000 out-of-school youth aged 14-16 and students aged 14-16 in Grade 6 or below) across six countries. The document does not specify an analytic subsample selection procedure (e.g., exclusions, completion thresholds, or missing-data rules) because no dataset is analyzed here.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD (2018) publication documents the assessment and analytical framework for PISA for Development (PISA-D), extending PISA 2012 and PISA 2015 frameworks for reading, mathematics, and science. It specifies that PISA-D aims to increase measurement resolution at the lower end of proficiency, broaden social and economic context coverage, and include an out-of-school component to better represent 14–16 year-olds who are not captured by standard school-based PISA sampling. The school-based assessment is paper-based (two hours total) with clustered test booklets and a 35-minute student background questionnaire, while the out-of-school assessment is tablet-based (50 minutes) with a core module and adaptive routing to forms, plus questionnaires for youth, a knowledgeable adult, and an interviewer. It also outlines the contextual questionnaire framework using the Education Prosperity model, emphasizing equality and equity and enhanced measurement of socio-economic status and poverty. Because this is a framework document, it does not report empirical ML model performance or achievement estimates.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a framework/technical documentation for PISA-D rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. Consequently, there is no analytic dataset, no reported model training/evaluation, no PV handling or missing-data strategy for an estimation model, and no country-level analytic sample sizes. The sparse fields (e.g., total_students, n_students, ML techniques) reflect that the publication’s purpose is to define what will be assessed and how instruments and questionnaires are structured for future implementation and analysis.
